@jonahkeri @bruce_arthur @mashable bruce, what is the alternative? Better to have expensive transportation than none at all
@DJColdGold look up "profiteering"
@DJColdGold and "none at all" isn't the alternative
.@jonahkeri Without surge pricing, all the drivers stay home, and people get cabs they don't need. How does that make the city better off?
@bruce_arthur @DJColdGold You don't grasp how Uber works if you think its profiteering.
@bfs82466 yeah, i do
If you haven't already deleted the app: @jonahkeri: Uber is a pile of garbage.
*sigh* “@jonahkeri: Uber is a pile of garbage.
@jonahkeri stick to baseball
@pbsenerchia uber needs a hard cap like baseball.
“@jonahkeri: Uber is a pile of garbage. people hate on Uber but people keep using the service.
@ctw78 no
@needham_chris It's all about the fans, man.
Maybe, like, 2% above normal rates. “@needham_chris: @pbsenerchia uber needs a hard cap like baseball.”
@jonahkeri @dandrezner criticizing them for this is wrongheaded on so many levels. how many rides would be available if @uber didn't exist?
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri ppl love the market until it negatively impacts them...
@bruce_arthur So how is it profiteering? You prefer to require these independent drivers go to work during which circumstances?
@jonahkeri the least you can do is read the article you tweet and understand how and why their fares change.
@bruce_arthur Its not like some driver says "here's a great chance to make big money!"
@bruce_arthur guess it has elements of price gouging, but at least uber's price surges increase supply. also not "essential" good/service
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri people, i'm sure, imagine an apocalyptic scenario where transport is scarce, rich escape, and poor die (1/2)
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri in such a scenario, the villain is not uber, but the driver who keep the meter running when life is at stake (2/2)
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Surge pricing is great. Using and then bragging about it when lives are at stake is disgusting.
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber *are* lives at stake?
@bmainou I don't
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner Assuming yes, for sake of argument, who's morally culpable: @Uber or drivers who base decisions upon it?
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber is designed to solve a problem about maximizing efficiency under normal circumstances.
@ctw78 is it inconceivable that someone could read the article, understand the laws of supply and demand, and still disagree with practices?
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber In extraordinary circumstances, we apply different moral criteria.
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Drivers *always* have the moral agency to offer to give rides for free, regardless of surge pricing
@jonahkeri I just deleted the ap. This is BS.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Except the irony is that the people helped by the surge pricing are the people Jonah thinks it hurts: The consumers.
@jonahkeri beyond price gouging, their use of user data has been poor at best too. Why use this service again?
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber So, to put it bluntly, fuck your moral highground. This event says 0 about ethics of surge pricing
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri The choice isn't regular prices or surge prices, it's surge prices or no cabs able to pick desperate people up.
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber The hostages certainly are. This isn't New Year's Eve or a broken train.
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber The hostages are not able to get into an uber, are they?
@bmainou yes
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Could uber offer to give a free ride to relatives of the hostages who want to get to safety? sure
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Is it reasonable to expect them to give everyone cheap rides just in case a relative wants one? No.
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Cheap? How about regular pricing considering people are fleeing an active gunman.
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Like I said, moral obligation of drivers to give rides to those in danger is independent of pricing
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber whole point of surge pricing is: many want 2 be w family now. Why *ration* rides now of all times?
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber This is a really really important basic point in economics that most people do not seem to grasp
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber You are really, really passionate about Uber's marginal revenue in the midst of a crisis.
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber I don't give a shit about their marginal revenue. I think ur proposal makes scared people worse off
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber It decreases the supply of rides for desperate people when they are most needed
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber While not achieving any of the egalitarian objectives you think it accomplishes
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Plus I don't have any information to suggest that people other than the hostages are in danger
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Nope, wrong because you ignore supply. More drivers are not going to appear because fares are higher.
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber This does not increase the supply of drivers, only raises the piece for scared riders.
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber That's almost certainly false. But only Uber has data 2 say, so at least your assertion is unfounded
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Why are you so confident about this? People respond to incentives in so many situations
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Driver probably wants to be w/ his or her family. But if price is high he/she might decide otherwise
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber The higher the price more likely such a decision would be made. Why do u think ur price is "better"?
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber No more confident than you are. I'm also done arguing about a company making extra profit in a crisis.
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Agree this is a minor issue in the grand scheme of things. But you're still Wrong On The Internet
@sflicht @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber And it only took you 983 tweets to say that.
@jonahkeri I’m not sure I understand what there is to disagree w/. As your article says fares “automatically” increase when supply<demand
@pat_stack @jonahkeri @dandrezner @Uber Well as u might surmise it's an issue I think people r consistently wrong about in a pernicious way
@jonahkeri do you think they are garbage for encouraging more drivers to get to the area to get people out? More drivers > less drivers
@jonahkeri in all fairness it looks like they might have updated the story after you tweeted and before I read it… Maybe the case…
@ctw78 All good. And debate is a good thing.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri why would there be no cabs?
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Because when a terrorist attack happens, there's a huge surge in demand, and drivers want to stay home. Big shortage.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri In an emergency, you need a system to encourage drivers on the road and make sure only the really needy grab cabs.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri The only way to do that is with pricing mechanisms (i.e. "surge pricing"). It's not immoral, it's amoral.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri meh I assume the drivers want to make $$. Leveraging a terrorist attack to raise prices is signs of unregulated biz
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri yes...because only the ppl with the $$ are the "really needy"...such a non real life way to look at things
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri It has nothing to do with drivers being greedy. It's a computer code. It's pure #math.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Why aren't you mad at the regular yellow cab drivers who refuse to pick anyone up in Sydney today?
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri If they all voluntarily went and did their jobs, there would be no shortage of demand and no surge in prices.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Uber is doing what the yellow cabs won't: Figuring out a way to get people transportation during an emergency.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri After Hurricane Sandy, NY and NJ refused "surge pricing" of gasoline. The result? Nobody could buy gasoline.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri When you try to pass laws banning the free market, the result is a shortage. You can't defeat supply & demand.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Prices are not punishment, they are INFORMATION. Without them, markets become dysfunctional. See: Union, Soviet.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri you still haven't explained why the needy ones are the rich people who can afford the costs
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri Uber is acting as if they have no choice...they have a choice
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri What is the choice? How do you get enough drivers to pick everybody up without surge pricing?
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Yellow cab drivers are refusing to go pick people up because they won't get paid extra for it. What's your solution?
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Poor people won't be able to get a cab when there's a supply shortage either. That's what you have to understand.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri In NYC, the gov't has a strict cab limit. The result is that yellow cabs only hang out near rich, white people.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri You can walk around the poor neighborhoods in the Bronx for hours. You will NEVER see a yellow cab. Never.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Free markets help the poor. They create supply where otherwise there would be nothing but shortages.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri what does day to day at the Bronx have to do with a specific terrorist situation?
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Both are the same to economists: A supply shortage due to an external intervention in the market.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri When there are supply shortages, those who have supply prefer to be around rich people. The poor get nothing.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri When there's 1 cab for every 10 people who want to get picked up in Sydney, who do they think gets picked up?
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri I'll give you a hint: it's probably not the impoverished minority. It's the rich, white guy in a business suit.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri And the beauty of surge pricing is that it immediately gets a bunch of people in a car, and then prices will drop.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Some rich, desperate people get cabs for $100, and then within a half hour prices drop down to normal levels.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri agree...in times that are outside of human nature everyone should only make rational based decisions...
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri The high prices will create a surge in supply. Or we can go back to your plan, where no poor people ever get picked up
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri it's like when all those doctors without borders do what the market says and donates their supplies to poor ppl
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Some very nice people do charity work for free. But expect every business to provide free products and despair.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri It's nice to imagine a world where everybody works voluntarily and nobody gets paid. But you get North Korea/Cambodia.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri And by the way, people are free to do that in Sydney RIGHT NOW. Uber's prices will drop immediately in response.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri I agree man...what other choice does Uber have in this rare and random instance....
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri you were doing so well with rational arguments and then you pulled this. Disappointing
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Pulling... what? It's a simple example of what happens when you remove price mechanisms.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Charity is wonderful. But pretending the whole world can work on charity rather than free markets is fantasy land.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Encourage people to do as much charity as possible, then let the marketplace fill in the gaps.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri you continue to compare day to day events to a rare unprecedented event. I know a way to cut Uber fares by 20%
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri They are the same to economists. It's all just math. You're trying to find moral meaning in math equations.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri and by your argument wouldn't impact supply at all.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri If you know a way to drop Uber fares by 20% without a supply shortage, start an Uber alternative. Make a business.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri arguing that moral info doesn't impact human decisions is extremely naive.
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Nobody says it doesn't. But in the end, the price that sets supply = demand takes all of that information into account
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri all Uber has to do is not take their 20% cut in these Situations.
@JeffWaksman @jonahkeri same pay to drivers so they're helping "get drivers on the street"
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri But then why would they provide a service if they're not making any money?
@blykmyk44 @jonahkeri Uber has administrators that have to work/get paid. Asking them to lose money today is asking them to shut down.

text: Quiet where I am. Lots of talking. Lots of standing. No smash-smash. #Ferguson
comments: One of the stranger elements of covering all this is seeing major demonstrations expressed in a suburban context.
In cities you rally in parks, in squares. Tahrir. Maidan. Zucotti. Here, we're standing in the street, outside a QuikTrip.
And I realize that's partly because the street has become a square. Because the police have partially boxed it in.
We don't really have pedestrian squares in the US, only a l'il in NYC @mattdpearce
Would we be here if the police weren't here? Or is the QuikTrip a de facto park because it's burned down, and no longer corporate space.
Well, here we are, and nobody's kicking us out, exactly. So. Suburban public space.
Very profound question/observation. @mattdpearce
